name: Ryan ST / PT-22 Recruit
summary: Sleek 1930s low-wing sport trainer, with the Kinner-powered PT-22 Recruit as the USAAF primary trainer; widely used as a sport and aerobatic airplane today.

wings: Thin, clean low wing with rounded tips
engines: Small five-cylinder Kinner radial with exposed cylinders (ST3KR / PT-22) or an inline (STA)
fuselage: Open tandem cockpits with a small windscreen for each seat
Narrow, shapely fuselage that tapers smoothly
Fixed gear with large streamlined wheel spats
tail: Rounded horizontal tail with a trim look

tellTales: Slender low-wing monoplane with open tandem cockpits and big wheel spats
Short nose with a small five-cylinder radial (or slim inline)
Clean, thin wing and very trim, sporty fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The Cornell has a longer nose, wider wing centre section and plainer main gear; the Ryan is smaller, trimmer and often has wheel spats.
The BT-13 is much bigger and heavier with a large radial and an enclosed greenhouse; the Ryan is a small open-cockpit trainer.
The Stearman is a biplane; the Ryan is a low-wing monoplane.
The N3N is a biplane; the Ryan is a low-wing monoplane.
